To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) existing robustness certificates for graph neural networks are overly pessimistic, (2) we propose the first collective certificate for graph neural networks, and (3) it can be used to drastically improve robustness.

(i) Graph Neural Networks have a locality property which allows to combine single node adversarial robustness guarantees into collective guarantees; (ii) This collective robustness certificate increases the number of certifiable adversarial examples by orders of magnitude; (iii) The collective certificate can be computed in polynomial time and is thus practical.
We introduce the first robustness certificate for multiple predictions of a graph neural network, i.e. we consider the robustness of the entire output vector instead of a single prediction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How to exploit interdependence in graph neural networks? What is the impact of collective robustness certificates on existing adversarial robustness benchmarks? How can we improve the efficiency of collective robustness certificate computation?
improving the robustness of graph neural networks.
improving the adversarial robustness of graph neural networks and other multi-label models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper presents a method for certifying adversarial robustness in graph neural networks.
we propose a new robustness certificate for Graph Neural Networks that exploits interdependencies between predictions and thus significantly strengthens the guarantees.

we propose the first collective certificate for graph neural networks, which is based on the locality property of GNNs, which is the first certificate that considers multiple predictions simultaneously and is thus much stronger than existing single-prediction certificates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we exploit the interdependence of predictions to obtain a much stronger certificate than existing ones.

the locality of graph neural networks enables us to leverage interdependence in the predictions to obtain collective robustness certificates that are significantly more efficient than the naive approach of considering each prediction independently.
for a single graph, a single image, or a single document, we are able to certify the robustness of many predictions, instead of only a single prediction as in prior works.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can exploit interdependence between predictions to significantly strengthen existing robustness certificates.
the interdependence of multiple predictions can be leveraged to drastically strengthen robustness certificates.
interdependence between multiple predictions can be exploited to drastically improve the robustness of a classifier, even if each prediction is individually vulnerable to adversarial attacks.
